issues.description: The problem specification / UML declares checkOrderReady() as returning void, while the provided solution implements checkOrderReady() with a boolean return type. This mismatch can confuse students about the expected method signature and return value they should implement to match the specification and tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method signature consistent with the problem specification: change the solution's checkOrderReady() to return void (and keep its internal behaviour identical), or alternatively update the problem statement and UML to specify a boolean return type. Also ensure the template and any tests expect the same signature.
